items.title: iPhone Duo: Folding Tablet Targets Niche Market
points: Apple's iPhone Duo is a foldable device that transforms from phone to miniature tablet.
Primary audience: commuters and business travelers seeking portable tablet functionality on trains, buses, and planes.
Standard smartphone users may find it frustrating due to average phone performance when not in tablet mode.

items.title: SpaceX Gains Military Tracking Access Amid Privatization Push
points: US military has granted SpaceX access to restricted space tracking data previously controlled by federal agencies.
Elon Musk's DOGE program eliminated federal space traffic control staff in 2025 and attempted budget cuts to the Traffic Coordination System for Space department.
Industry observers view these moves as an attempt to privatize Earth orbit traffic control, raising national security and competitive fairness questions.
Action consolidates control of critical space infrastructure with a single private contractor receiving special government access.

items.title: High-Frequency Traders Compete for AI Computing Power
points: Trading firms like Jane Street are investing heavily in compute capacity and faster chips as competitive advantages.
These firms profit from tiny price differences (basis points: one hundredth of a percent) by entering and exiting positions at extreme speed.
Increasing reliance on machine learning algorithms means trading success directly correlates with computing power available.
Firms face pressure to invest despite significant risks, viewing compute acquisition as essential to avoid obsolescence.

items.title: Neural Chip Breakthrough Reads Inter-Brain Communication
points: Implantable chip records activity and extracts biomarkers describing brain wave strength and synchronization between different brain regions.
Machine-learning algorithm decodes signals to distinguish between cognitive and emotional states with clinical precision.
Ability to trigger precisely timed stimulation based on brain-network biomarkers opens applications in treatment and brain-computer interfaces.
Technology represents a significant advance in understanding and potentially intervening in neurological conditions.

items.title: How a GitHub Staff Engineer Estimates 'Impossible' Work
points: Read the room first: gauge how much pressure is behind the request before estimating.
Start with the target deadline and work backwards to find a version of the project that fits.
Price in unknowns: build buffer for unfamiliar parts of the codebase ('dark forests') or reshape the plan to use known components.
Offer 2-3 options with different risk tradeoffs so managers can choose (tight timeline vs. rushing risky parts vs. adding team members).
Reserve 'this is impossible' for truly infeasible cases to keep stakeholders listening.

items.title: Moonshot's Kimi K3.1 Pro Closes In on Frontier Coding Models
points: Scored 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, beating GPT-6 Astra and trailing just behind Claude Opus 5.5.
Features a 1M-token context window (can process up to 1 million words in a single request) and handles long-horizon coding tasks including bug fixes and building games in Unity and Godot.
Priced at $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, undercutting major competitors.
Hacking-related data was deliberately removed from training to limit offensive cyber capabilities; open weights arriving by November 4.

items.title: Tailscale SSH Flaws Enable Server Compromise
points: Researcher Erica Windisch published details on 11 security flaws in Tailscale software and self-hosted headscale server affecting SSH access.
Proof-of-concept showed one hacked device could abuse SSH port forwarding (tunneling connections between machines) to gain full control of other machines and inject rogue devices into the network.
No patch is yet available; Tailscale says fixes are coming but recommends auditing SSH access and disabling unnecessary port forwarding in the interim.

items.title: iPad mini Gets First OLED Screen
points: New 8.5-inch OLED screen (larger than previous LCD model) offers more than double the peak brightness and sharper contrast.
Design is 5.4mm thick, 15% thinner than prior version, with A20 Pro chip, Wi-Fi 7, water resistance, and an optional $100 anti-glare nano-texture screen.
Pre-orders start Wednesday at 10:10 a.m. Pacific; in stores Friday November 6 starting at $699 in Midnight and Starlight colors.

items.title: Meta Raises $95B to Fund AI Infrastructure
points: Meta's largest stock offering since 2013, including $60 billion via newly created nonvoting shares that let CEO Zuckerberg raise capital without losing voting control.
Hyperscalers (large-scale cloud computing providers) are expected to spend roughly $800 billion on AI this year and over $1 trillion next year.
Meta shares rose 2% on the news, reflecting how expensive the AI race has become for companies competing at scale.

items.title: Musk Admits Deliberate Starlink Slowdown in Ukraine
points: Musk acknowledged slowing Starlink last week, claiming Ukraine's military used the service for offensive drone strikes against terms of service.
Slowdown affected Starshield (military version of Starlink), cutting connections for drones and aircraft moving faster than 100 mph across most of the country.
Senator Adam Schiff called for a Senate investigation and demanded Musk testify under oath after a Wall Street Journal report of his direct order.

items.title: OpenAI Slashes Pricing to Poach Anthropic Customers
points: OpenAI cut prices by 30-90% to win over customers from Anthropic.
Major companies are redirecting AI budgets in response to the price cuts.

items.title: AI Profits Concentrated in Magnificent 7
points: Apollo economist Torsten Slok found AI revenue and profit gains isolated to the Magnificent 7 (Alphabet, Amazon, Apple, Meta, Microsoft, Nvidia, Tesla), while the other 493 S&P 500 firms show zero financial improvement.

Magnificent 7 companies earn about $780,000 revenue per worker at ~30% margins, versus $525,000 and 10% margins for the rest of the market; many firms now treat token costs as an operational drag and are reducing spending.
The top 10% of firms control 99.5% of model inference spending and 95% of AI vendor spending (on providers like OpenAI and Anthropic).

sections.title: How a GitHub Staff Engineer Estimates Impossible Work
points: 1. Read the room first: gauge how much pressure is actually behind the request before estimating; a CTO's one-week deadline needs a different answer than a casual ask.
2. Start with the target: ask what version of the project could fit the timeline already on the table, then work backwards from there.
3. Price in the unknowns: build extra buffer for 'dark forests' in your codebase, or reshape the plan to use parts your team knows well.
4. Give people choices: offer 2-3 options with different risk levels so managers can pick the tradeoff (tight timeline vs. rushing risky parts vs. bringing in new team members).
5. Earn trust by rarely saying 'this is impossible'—people stop listening if you push back on every estimate, so reserve that response for cases where it truly is infeasible.

points: 1. Kimi K3.1 Pro scored 65.7% on Terminal-Bench 4.0, putting it ahead of GPT-6 Astra and just behind Claude Opus 5.5.

3. Pricing is $2 per million input tokens and $10 per million output tokens, undercutting major competitors.
4. Deliberately removed hacking-related data from training to limit offensive cyber capabilities; open weights arriving by November 4.
